topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, relates the content to histopathology practicals, and outlines the day's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the historical study of transmissible tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular oncogenes and the development of assays to measure transformed cellular phenotypes.

topics.label: Functional classifications and mechanisms of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer mutations are functionally classified and illustrate the contrasting mechanisms of oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and dominant negative alleles in cell cycle control.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: They distinguish between sequence and chromosomal instability and explore the specific DNA repair, replication, and mitotic defects that generate them.

topics.label: Stepwise tumor evolution and hereditary cancer syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: They address how the sequential accumulation of inherited and somatic mutations accelerates tumorigenesis and influences cancer predisposition.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session with a recap of learning outcomes, recommended background reading, and framing for the upcoming lecture.
